title: The Father and His Sons
source: Aesop's Fables, tr. G. F. Townsend (1867), 'The Father and His Sons'
lesson: Together you are strong; divided, you break.
lines: A father had three sons who argued all day long. About chores, about food, about absolutely everything.
He told them to stop. He begged them to stop. Nothing worked. So he tried something different.
He tied a bundle of sticks together, and said: break this. The first son pushed. The second son pulled. The third son sat on it.
Not one of them could break the bundle. Then the father untied it, and handed each son a single stick.
Snap, snap, snap. Each stick broke as easily as a breadstick.
My sons, said the father, if you stand together, no enemy can break you. But if you fight each other, you will snap, one by one, just like these sticks.
Together you are strong; divided, you break. So the next time you argue with your family, remember the bundle.
